SIP-1: Block Trade
A system that announces large positions on-chain and matches them with multiple counterparties. It enables institutional-sized execution without affecting price discovery.
SIP-2: Position Yield
A time-based yield distribution on open positions. The longer and healthier you hold your position, the more you earn from protocol revenues.

SIP-3: Position Transfer
The ability to transfer your position directly to another trader instead of closing it on the market.
I think the next step could be making the position itself tradable.  @jimmyitsopen 

The buyer would enter the position from your entry level, while you exit without being tied to instant market conditions, on your own terms.
This is not just about slippage. It also means having control over your exit.
You don’t have to think about whether to wait for TP, you can realize your profit early.
If the position is already in profit, you could even try to transfer it at a price slightly above your current profit.

For example, you might be a trader who prefers quick in-and-out trades. When you see an opportunity, you enter, take your profit, and exit.
But on the other side, there may be someone who reads the market more broadly and prefers to hold positions for a longer period.

They would want to enter at the best possible level. Your position becomes a ready and advantageous entry for them.
Instead of chasing the market from scratch, they enter from a level that has already been tested.
This way, one trader completes their trade quickly, while the other secures a quality entry.
In practice, instead of placing orders into the market, traders move forward by taking over each other’s positions.

The next step of this could evolve further.
Positions opened with strong entries become more valuable, and over time a position marketplace could emerge.
